html:
John the Blind was Count of Luxembourg and King of Bohemia, born in 1296. He is the best known ruler of medieval Luxembourg and a national hero there.

He was the son of the emperor Henry VII, and his marriage in 1310 won him the crown of Bohemia. The House of Luxembourg went on to give the Holy Roman Empire several kings and emperors, among them his son Charles IV.

John spent his life on campaign across Europe and lost his sight in middle age. In 1346 he rode, blind, into the Battle of Crécy on the French side and was killed. The Schueberfouer fair he founded in 1340 is still held in Luxembourg City each summer.
